text:
oncall-bot: ALERT: 1812 hosts in us-west-2 reporting increased 504/gateway timeouts for /v1/generate. error_rate 5xx > 4% in last 5m, p95 latency x2. Tagging #incidents — page to oncall.
alyssa: seeing a handful of customer escalations (ACME, BrightBay). they report requests hang ~30s then 504. raising here. any immediate fixes? :grimacing:
devon: thanks. i see queue_depth metric for hosted-inference-prod in us-west peaking at ~980/1000. max_queue_depth is configured 1000 for that pool. queue_wait_ms p95 jumped to 1800ms then to 5200ms.
mike: logs show continuous-batcher backlog growing. batcher_enqueue_duration has long tail. some batches are being split into tiny single-token batches which is killing throughput.
sarah: can we confirm whether early_reject is enabled for these routes? if not, gateway keeps queuing until client timeout which leads to 504s.
alyssa: support ticket #SUP-2419 from ACME has traces: last_event id trace-0a7c shows repeated 504s across two regions. their pattern: high concurrency from a few api keys + very long sequence_length ~12k tokens.
jordan: that long sequences strain KV cache and block the token loop. continuous batching backlog + very large seq lengths => tail latencies.
linda-support: customer is asking for timeline and mitigation; they're very sensitive (paid dedicated plan but currently on hosted). need immediate temporary workarounds.
infra-bot: deploybot: autoscaler triggered +3 GPU workers at 14:02:13 UTC, but backlog didn't clear due to queue depth hitting limit and early_reject=false.
devon: short term mitigation options: 1) enable early_reject on hosted pool for public API to drop requests once queue_depth >= 900, 2) reduce max_batch_size for the pool to prevent huge single batches, 3) route heavy-key customers to a smaller model variant or dedicated tenant if possible.
mike: i can flip early_reject flag now. would prefer to announce to support so customers get 429 instead of 504. 429 is clearer.
alyssa: go ahead. also can we throttle the offending api keys (key ids from ticket: key-ak-ACMEXYZ). we should put temporary rate-limit on them while we investigate.
devon: executing toggle:
```
infra-cli --env prod pool update --name hosted-usw2 --set early_reject=true --set early_reject_threshold=900
```
devon: toggled early_reject=true at 14:05:02 UTC. monitoring.
mike: added temporary rate-limit: 60 qps for key-ak-ACMEXYZ via gateway rules. support notified customer.
sarah: metrics update: within 2 minutes 5xx rate dropped from 4.1% -> 0.6%. queue_depth median fell to 320, p95 latency back to baseline ~220ms. tail latency still elevated p99 ~2.2s for some traces.
alyssa: customer confirmed fewer 504s but they'd like root cause. we should collect repro and logs.
jordan: repro steps we used in staging to replicate:
1) stream 8 concurrent clients with sequence_length ~10k each
2) send synchronous generate calls without streaming chunking
3) ramp QPS to 300 over 30s
curl example:
```
for i in {1..8}; do 
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer key-ak-ACMEXYZ" \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"input":"<10k prompt ...>","max_tokens":2000}' &
done
```
jordan: in staging we saw batcher queue depth saturate and enqueue_wait_ms for some requests > 10s, which then triggered client timeouts.
linda-support: adding this to SUP-2419 as repro steps and telling ACME we recommend they chunk long contexts or use streaming.
devon: collecting more logs. critical log snippet showing backlog timing:
```
[14:03:58] request_id=aq-7f enqueue_time_ms=5320 queue_depth=982 batch_id=b-174
[14:03:59] request_id=aq-8a enqueue_time_ms=1120 queue_depth=988 batch_id=b-175
[14:04:01] request_id=aq-9c enqueue_time_ms=7340 queue_depth=996 batch_id=b-176
```
mike: note: some worker GC cycles coincided with backlog spikes. we saw 2 oom_kill attempts earlier this week on host gpu-44. suspect memory pressure when servicing large sequences.
sarah: post-mortem checklist items:
- tune batching config: cap per-request token length for batching decision, avoid grouping large seqs with short ones
- enforce per-key concurrency limits at gateway
- implement soft-fail/429 policy for sustained queue_depth pressure
- add better telemetry: per-request enqueue_time_ms exported to support traces
- consider model-variant fallback auto-route (smaller model under pressure)
devon: created follow-up infra ticket INFRA-1257 to add a circuit-breaker that rejects requests once queue_wait_ms > 3s for X% of recent requests.
jordan: also need a knob to cap kv-cache memory per-request or evict long-context caches faster.
alyssa: what's next for the customer? linda-support, please share incident summary and ETA for fixes.
linda-support: replied to ACME: temporary rate limit in place; we enabled early_reject to return 429 for overloaded requests; recommend chunking or smaller contexts; escalated to product for long-term solution. ETA for infra fixes 2 weeks (INFRA-1257 + batching changes).
infra-bot: NOTE: scheduled rolling restart of batcher pool tomorrow 03:00 UTC to pick up GC improvements — will announce in eng-runtime channel.
mike: follow-up: we should also add a canary that simulates heavy long-context traffic to detect config regressions earlier.
sarah: agreed. i'll own a short postmortem doc and link SUP-2419 + INFRA-1257. will include timelines, mitigations, replay steps, and customer communication draft.
alyssa: thanks all. good work triaging quickly. marking incident resolved for now; monitoring for regression. :thumbsup:
